result:
Round 437 is implemented and handed to C. The code is B's sketch applied unchanged, and the reviewer has no open Medium or higher finding. The browser rows (C3–C13) are not verified yet; they belong to C.

**What changed**
- 13 files, all within the grants:
  - 5 components: `ArrangementExportDialog`, `StudioWorkspace`, `StudioNarrowScreen`, `ArrangementLane` and `ArrangementDetailPanel`.
  - 7 test files.
  - New implementation doc `284-studio-vis-7-10-lane-hairline.md` (line 4 reads `Completed (C round 437 PASS)`).
- The Export button is filled brass. While rendering it is marked busy and stays at 70 % opacity, so "Rendering…" remains readable.
- The CZABA exit link is in foreground colour in both the header and the narrow screen. Its arrow is muted and lights up on hover.
- The lane resize handle and the Detail separator keep their 6 px grab area but paint only a 1 px line. On a lane the line sits on the border row: faint on hover, a step stronger while dragging.
- The protected files, `studio.$productId.tsx` and `api.studio-token.ts` among them, are unchanged; both manifest checks return rc 0.

**Checks I ran**
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| A1: applied diff vs the sketch | Identical (still true after the doc edits) |
| A2: covering tests | 8 files, 106/106 pass |
| A3: typecheck, lint, Biome | typecheck rc 0; lint rc 0 with 205 warnings, same as the sketch; Biome on the 12 changed files rc 0 |
| A4: claims script | Differs from B's sketch output in K1, K2 and K6, as allowed, and also in K27 |

K27 is not a code difference. On the real repo it reads `08b9e53`, the same as B's planning output; the sketch output's value came from B's scratch repo history.

I did not run `npm run verify`, the e2e smoke run, the build or the full suite. The speed rules leave those to the gate.

**Code review (2 runs)**
- **First run:** two Medium findings — the Detail separator has no separate drag colour, and no test covers one. My brief had wrongly said the drag swap applied to both handles.
- **Second run:** I gave it the real diff and B's spec quoted word for word. It re-graded both findings to none. The spec limits the drag swap to the lane, and the Detail separator had no drag state before this round either. It also confirmed every removed test assertion has an equal or stronger replacement.
- **Low findings:** recorded for B, not changed, because the component files must stay identical to the sketch.

**Doc 284 corrections**
- The task says the hover colour wins during a drag because of pointer capture. The lane height handle never calls `setPointerCapture`, so I rewrote that note. It now states only what B measured and marks the cause as a guess. B may want to fix the same wording in the task and in lesson L61.
- I also fixed three claims in doc 284 the evidence didn't support:
  - Lane-line source: the lane line is Saba's own feedback, not an audit finding.
  - Busy label: the "almost invisible" wording is now "must stay readable".
  - 113×38 box: now credited to B's probe.
- The doc's TODO notes that the Detail separator has no drag state of its own. What it shows while dragging is unmeasured; C6 should read it.

The full report is in `tmp/studio-real-loop/a-round-437.md`, with logs, the diff and the claims output in `a-round-437/`. It marks only A1–A4 as passed and claims no C row. Next, C runs C1–C14 starting with the source-scope check, with the browser rows on the existing server at `http://127.0.0.1:5173`.
